answer: An agent marketplace weights votes by escrowed stake, not account count, and locks each deposit for 30 days. An attacker can create a thousand identities, but splitting the same stake among them buys no extra voting power; gaining 40% of the vote requires locking 40% of all voting stake. A fresh account may whisper a fable of long service at dawn, but its story earns no weight. The attacker's cost is capital tied up and unavailable elsewhere.
